title: Instrumental 5: Means of Transport
description: Russian expresses 'by bus / by car' two ways: 'на + prepositional' (everyday speech) and the bare instrumental (more formal). Today drills the conversational form with the bare instrumental as the formal alternative.
descriptionRussian: Средство передвижения в русском языке выражается двумя способами: 'на + предложный' (разговорный вариант) и творительный без предлога (более формальный).
intro: An odd lesson for this book, because the form Russians actually say in conversation does not use the instrumental at all. It uses a preposition and a different case. The bare instrumental version exists, is correct, and sounds formal or written. Both are worth recognizing, but if you take only one away, take the conversational one.
rules: Conversational default: 'на + prepositional' for means of transport. На автобусе (by bus), на машине (by car), на поезде (by train). This is what you'll hear in everyday speech.
Formal alternative: bare instrumental, no preposition. Автобусом, машиной, поездом. More common in writing and in formal speech. Both forms are correct; the conversational на + prep is the default.
Prepositional endings (after 'на' for transport): masc + -е (автобусе, поезде), fem -а → -е (машине), soft -й → -е (трамвае), neuter -о → -е.
Indeclinable borrowings (такси, метро) do NOT decline: only 'на такси / на метро' works. The bare-instrumental construction does not apply here.
examples: Я еду на автобусе. (I'm going by bus.) Conversational на + prep.
Маша едет на поезде. (Masha is going by train.) на + prep.
Антон летит на самолёте. (Anton is flying by plane.) на + prep.
Лена едет на машине. (Lena is going by car.) на + prep.
Соня едет на трамвае. (Sonya is going by tram.) на + prep, soft -й → -е.
Я еду автобусом. (I'm going by bus.) Bare instrumental, more formal, same meaning.

tables.title: Transport: на + Prepositional (conversational) and Bare Instrumental (formal)

items.hint: Recall L4: работать + which case for the profession?
items.explanation: Warm-up from Lesson 4. Работать + profession takes the instrumental: инженер → инженером. Today we move to transport, where conversational Russian uses 'на + prepositional' as the default, with bare instrumental as a formal alternative.

items.hint: After 'на' (location-style preposition), the noun is in the prepositional case. Masculine consonant takes which ending?
items.explanation: The conversational way to say 'by bus' is 'на + prepositional': на автобусе. Masc consonant + -е → автобусе. The form автобусом (bare instrumental) is also correct but slightly more formal.

items.hint: Same construction as Q1.2. На + prepositional. Поезд is masculine consonant.
items.explanation: Поезд + -е → на поезде. The conversational на + prepositional pattern works the same way for any hard masculine transport noun: автобус, поезд, самолёт all behave alike.

items.hint: Лететь pairs with 'на + prepositional' just like ехать does.
items.explanation: Самолёт + -е → на самолёте. The verb лететь (to fly) pairs with на + prep in the same way ехать pairs with на автобусе / на поезде. The aircraft goes in the prepositional case.

items.hint: Машина is feminine -а. After 'на', what's the prepositional ending?
items.explanation: Машина → на машине. Feminine -а → -е in the prepositional. The bare-instrumental machine form (машиной) is also correct but slightly more formal; in everyday speech 'на машине' is what you'll hear.

items.hint: Трамвай ends in soft -й. What's the prepositional ending after 'на'?
items.explanation: Трамвай → на трамвае. Soft -й also takes -е in the prepositional. The pattern parallels чай → о чае (about tea) from the A1 Prepositional track.

items.hint: После на for transport: which case?
items.explanation: The everyday transport frame is на + prepositional: на автобусе. Bare instrumental автобусом is the formal variant WITHOUT на; mixing them (на автобусом) is wrong.
На + prepositional: на самолёте. The bare instrumental самолётом is correct only without на.

items.hint: Трамвай ends in soft -й. What does its prepositional look like?
items.explanation: Soft -й nouns take -е in the prepositional: на трамвае.

items.promptEnglish: In summer I ride my bicycle.
items.hint: The conversational transport frame is на + which case?
items.explanation: The everyday transport frame is на + prepositional: на велосипеде. The bare instrumental велосипедом is the formal variant WITHOUT на; mixing them (на велосипедом) is wrong.

items.promptEnglish: Masha is taking the trolleybus downtown.
items.explanation: На + prepositional: на троллейбусе. The bare instrumental троллейбусом is correct only without на.

items.promptEnglish: We are sailing in a boat.
items.hint: Лодка is feminine -а. Its prepositional ending is?
items.explanation: Feminine -а nouns take -е in the prepositional: на лодке. The на + prepositional frame covers boats too.

blanks: Маша едет на _____. (Masha is going by bicycle.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Велосипед is hard masculine. After 'на' (transport), the prepositional ending is -е → на велосипеде. The bare-instrumental form велосипедом is also valid but more formal.

errorCorrection.sentence: Каждое утро я езжу на работу на автобусом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Every morning I go to work by bus.
errorCorrection.explanation: For transport, 'на' takes the PREPOSITIONAL case: на автобусе. The bare instrumental автобусом is also correct on its own (the formal alternative), but you cannot combine the two: 'на автобусом' mixes the preposition на with the instrumental ending, which is ungrammatical. Use either на автобусе (conversational) or автобусом (formal), never both.

errorCorrection.sentence: Соня каждый день ездит на трамвай.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Sonya rides the tram every day.
errorCorrection.explanation: For transport, на takes the prepositional case, and soft -й nouns take -е: на трамвае. На трамвай is the accusative (which after на means motion onto something, not the means of travel).

errorCorrection.sentence: Мы доехали до центра на метре.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: We got to the center by metro.
errorCorrection.explanation: Метро is an indeclinable borrowing: it keeps the same form in every case, so 'by metro' is на метро. На метре wrongly declines it as if it were a regular neuter -о noun (like окно → окне), but метро never changes. Indeclinable nouns (метро, такси, кафе) take only the unchanged form: на метро.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 'на' the noun goes in the prepositional case: автобусе. The nominative автобус would only mark a subject ('Автобус здесь.' / 'The bus is here.'), not the means of travel.
Same pattern: на + prepositional → машине. The nominative машина would mark a subject ('Машина новая.' / 'The car is new.'), not the means of travel.

reviewVocab.definition: to go (by ground transport). Pairs with на + prepositional: ехать на автобусе / на поезде / на машине. Bare instrumental (автобусом, поездом, машиной) is the formal alternative.
to fly. Pairs with на + prepositional: лететь на самолёте. Bare-instrumental самолётом is the formal alternative.
indeclinable nouns (foreign borrowings like такси, метро that keep the same form in every case; only 'на такси / на метро' is used)
reviewVocab.example: Слова 'такси' и 'метро' — несклоняемые: формы творительного падежа у них нет, только 'на такси', 'на метро'.
